title: Google Ads MCP: connect Claude to your ad account (2026)

facts.fact: Anthropic released the Model Context Protocol (MCP), an open standard for connecting AI assistants to outside tools and data, in November 2024.
facts.quote: MCP is the open standard Anthropic released in November 2024 for connecting AI assistants to outside tools and data

facts.fact: Superscale AI's free plan includes 1,000 credits and does not require a credit card.
facts.quote: The free plan includes 1,000 credits with no card required.

facts.fact: According to Superscale AI, connecting ad accounts to Superscale requires the Pro plan at $199 per month or higher.
facts.quote: ad account integrations require the Pro plan at $199 per month or higher.

facts.fact: According to Superscale AI, the Advanced plan costs $99 and covers ad creation but not the ad account connection.
facts.quote: The Advanced plan at $99 covers ad creation but not the account connection.

facts.fact: According to Superscale AI, a Google Ads performance report run through the MCP costs 10 credits.
facts.quote: A report run costs 10 credits, a plain chat message 1

facts.fact: According to Superscale AI, a plain chat message costs 1 credit.
facts.quote: A report run costs 10 credits, a plain chat message 1

facts.fact: According to Superscale AI, each static image generated costs 30 credits.
facts.quote: Static images cost 30 credits each and agent video runs 500 credits per 15 seconds

facts.fact: According to Superscale AI, agent video runs cost 500 credits per 15 seconds.
facts.quote: agent video runs 500 credits per 15 seconds

facts.fact: Context that Claude passes from Notion or Google Drive to the Superscale agent is used only for that single run and is not saved back into the brand context, according to Superscale AI.
facts.quote: context passed this way is used for that single run and is not yet saved back into your brand context.

facts.fact: Superscale AI notes that Ryze's own MCP roundup ranks Ryze first among Google Ads MCP options.
facts.quote: Ryze's own MCP roundup ranks Ryze first, which tells you how these lists usually work.
